hydrated.howExcerpt: Lenders price the exit, not the asset. Example. Follow one position through four states. The numbers are the example from the hero: 300 mock NVDAx at $185, with $28,000 already drawn against the asset. Quotes and DEX depth are example figures; the LTV limits, the haircuts and the Reserve are the deployed testnet values. 01 A static lender stops at 40%. A tokenized stock can trade at fair value all week and have no buyer on Saturday night. Lenders price that exit, so the limit stays low. 02 Committed quotes raise the ceiling. Market makers escrow USDC behind quotes that can't leave without notice. In this example (quotes $80,000 and DEX depth $12,000 are example figures; the Reserve as deployed holds $10), the same 300 shares reach the deployed 70% cap. 03 The weekend guard tightens it on its own. When the market closes or the price is older than 15 minutes, DEX depth drops to zero and the haircut widens to 25%. Nothing outside the contract can switch the session back on. 04 A bad loan sells to a buyer who already committed. If health falls below 1, collateral goes to a committed quote at no more than its stated discount. The Reserve fills only after every quote is used. Example: 30
hydrated.panAExcerpt: // Borrow limit for one asset (spec §4.2). Integers only: _e6 USD, bps.pub fn borrow_limit_e6(&self, a: &Asset) -> u128 { let weekend = !self.guard.session_open(a); let h_bps = if weekend { a.h_weekend_bps } else { a.h_session_bps }; // 2500 / 1000 on testnet let d = if weekend { 0 } else { a.dex_depth_e6 }; let backing = a.quotes_e6 + a.reserve_e6 + d; // Q + R + D let by_exit = backing * (10_000 - h_bps) / 10_000; let by_ltv = a.value_e6() * a.ltv_max_bps / 10_000; // 70% on testnet // the exit term is shared by every loan in the asset by_ltv.min(by_exit.saturating_sub(a.total_debt_e6))}
